questiontext.text:
Consider the trigonometric equation \(\sin\theta = {@given_disp@}\).

Give all answers in degrees, correct to \(1\) decimal place. You may use a calculator.

(a) Determine the reference angle \(\alpha\).

\(\alpha = \) [[input:ans0]]\(^\circ\) [[validation:ans0]] [[feedback:prta]]

(b) Find all the values of \(\theta\) with \(0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ\) that satisfy the equation.

First solution: \(\theta = \) [[input:ans1]]\(^\circ\) [[validation:ans1]]
Second solution: \(\theta = \) [[input:ans2]]\(^\circ\) [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prtb]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

We are given \(\sin\theta = {@given_disp@}\).

Step 1: Determine the reference angle.

The reference angle \(\alpha\) is the acute angle whose sine is the size of the given value, ignoring the sign. Take the inverse sine of the absolute value (with the calculator in degree mode):

\[ \alpha = \sin^{-1}\left({@abs_disp@}\right) = {@alpha_disp@}^\circ \quad (\text{to 1 decimal place}). \]

Step 2: Identify the quadrants.

\(\sin\theta\) is negative. By the CAST rule, sine is positive only in Quadrants I and II, so it is negative in Quadrants III and IV. There is one solution in each.

Step 3: Determine the first solution.

In Quadrant III, the terminal side is \(\alpha\) past \(180^\circ\):

\[ \theta_1 = 180^\circ + \alpha = 180^\circ + {@alpha_disp@}^\circ = {@t1_disp@}^\circ. \]

Step 4: Determine the second solution.

In Quadrant IV, the terminal side is \(\alpha\) short of \(360^\circ\):

\[ \theta_2 = 360^\circ - \alpha = 360^\circ - {@alpha_disp@}^\circ = {@t2_disp@}^\circ. \]

Final answer:

\[ \theta = {@t1_disp@}^\circ \quad\text{or}\quad \theta = {@t2_disp@}^\circ. \]

Seeing the solutions. On the graph of \(y = \sin\theta\), the line \(y = {@given_disp@}\) crosses the curve exactly twice between \(0^\circ\) and \(360^\circ\), at the two solutions:

node.description: Solutions in Quadrants I and II

truefeedback.text: Those angles are in Quadrants I and II, where sine is positive. Here \(\sin\theta\) is negative: use the CAST rule to find the two quadrants where sine is negative.

falsefeedback.text: Sine is negative here, so the solutions are in Quadrants III and IV. Use \(\theta = 180^\circ + \alpha\) and \(\theta = 360^\circ - \alpha\).
